# Independent native-default rotation-cache confirmation

Discovery used 72 processes and produced +1.246% [0.157%, 2.346%] for cache versus the same private core disabled in 10 load-matched blocks. Cache versus stock was inconclusive. These results are not confirmation.

Before timing, build a separate private core from the pinned discovery source with one startup-only `LLAMA_CONST_ROT_CREATED` stderr marker per successful cache creation, gated independently of the per-bypass audit. Do not print during generation. Keep the disabled and enabled arms on the identical rebuilt core. Require the expected two creation markers for each enabled process, zero for disabled, and no fallback warnings; a missing marker invalidates the process. This marker demonstrates creation, while prior direct bypass witnesses and qualification cover the unchanged lookup path. Requalify the rebuilt core against stock using all five native-default raw-target cases, exact tokens and counters, and repeat-clear diagnostic before timing. Record all failures and no driver errors.

If qualification succeeds, predeclare 48 fresh processes in 12 balanced ABBA/BAAB blocks, 24 per arm, identical model, native defaults, driver, sampler, MTP, 512 requested tokens and backend to the discovery experiment. CPU/build/runnable matching, telemetry requirements, primary steady-throughput effect, descriptive t interval and at least four matched blocks are identical to the discovery protocol. Also report all blocks and generation, startup, memory and power; no tuning, pooling or reruns. A positive lower bound in the independent matched comparison supports the enabled-versus-disabled result for this configuration; it does not establish a stock gain or a faster mega kernel. Keep the system clocks untouched and serialize GPU jobs with the existing guard.
